comments.note: DesktopFileLauncherService.cs: The null-coalescing fallback `Path.GetDirectoryName(filePath) ?? filePath` in ShowInExplorer silently swallows the edge case where filePath is a root path (e.g. '/'). This is an extremely unlikely scenario in practice, but an early null-guard or argument validation at the method entry could make the intent explicit. Low priority — no known caller passes a root path.

DesktopFileLauncherService.cs: Process.Start() can return null if the OS refuses to create the process (e.g. xdg-open not found). The existing pattern of discarding the return value with `_ = Process.Start(psi)` silently swallows this — consistent with the existing Windows behaviour, but worth noting as a potential silent failure mode on Linux if xdg-open is absent.

comments.note: ShowInExplorer on Linux: Path.GetDirectoryName('/') returns null, triggering the ?? filePath fallback, which passes '/' to xdg-open. This opens the root directory — an acceptable silent fallback for an extremely unlikely caller scenario.

Process.Start(psi) can return null if xdg-open is not installed. Both methods discard the return value with '_ =', silently swallowing the failure. Consistent with Windows branch behavior and low risk in practice; xdg-open is available in all mainstream Linux desktop environments.

comments.note: A09 — Security Logging: Process.Start() return value is discarded with '_ =' in both OpenFolder and ShowInExplorer. If the OS fails to launch the process (e.g. xdg-open absent, explorer.exe unavailable), the failure is silently swallowed with no log entry. Not a security vulnerability in context, but worth noting as a silent failure mode. Consistent with the existing Windows pattern. File: src/VideoIndexer.App/Services/DesktopFileLauncherService.cs, lines 39 and 64.

A03 (Functional Edge Case) — ShowInExplorer on Windows constructs ArgumentList entry as $"/select,{filePath}" (line 51). ArgumentList prevents OS-level command injection correctly. However, if filePath contains an embedded comma (e.g. C:\videos,backup\movie.mp4), explorer.exe may misparse its own /select, argument internally. This is a functional edge case, not a security vulnerability — no code execution or privilege escalation is possible. File: src/VideoIndexer.App/Services/DesktopFileLauncherService.cs, line 51.

A08 (Info) — xdg-open is resolved from the user's $PATH at runtime. A malicious binary named xdg-open placed earlier in PATH would be invoked instead of the system utility. This is an environmental concern shared by all tools using PATH-based resolution; it requires prior local code execution (full user account compromise) and is not introduced by this change. No remediation required in this codebase. File: src/VideoIndexer.App/Services/DesktopFileLauncherService.cs, lines 30, 60.

[documentation-forward] DesktopFileLauncherService class-level XML doc states 'On Linux and other Unix-like systems, delegates to xdg-open.' The phrase 'other Unix-like systems' could imply macOS support, but xdg-open is a freedesktop.org/Linux utility and does not exist on macOS. The Documentation agent should tighten this to 'On Linux and other freedesktop.org-compatible systems' or simply 'On Linux' to avoid misleading future contributors. IFileLauncherService.cs interface docs are already accurate and need no change.
